Perfect! So sesh uses `.tar.gz` which doesn't need xz. Now let me verify one more thing - check if worktrunk has a tar.gz release or only tar.xz by looking at the GitHub releases URL structure (which is what the selectattr does):

Now let me create the comprehensive report with all my findings. Based on my thorough analysis, here's what I found:

## Investigation Report: Worktrunk XZ Installation Issue in noRoot Mode

### 1. ROOT CAUSE
The task at `/home/ldw/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml:2415` is **missing the `tags: [sudo]` annotation**. In noRoot mode, the ansible playbook runs with `--skip-tags sudo` (set in `run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl:249`), which should skip this task. However, since it lacks the tag, it still executes with `become: true`, triggering the `sudo: a password is required` error.

### 2. EXACT YAML BLOCK — WORKTRUNK INSTALL SECTION

**File:** `/home/ldw/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml`  
**Lines:** 2405–2536

```yaml
# --- worktrunk (git worktree manager for parallel AI agents) ---
- name: Check if worktrunk is installed
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
  ansible.builtin.command: wt --version
  register: worktrunk_check
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false
  environment:
    PATH: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin:/usr/local/bin:{{ ansible_facts['env']['PATH'] }}"

- name: Ensure xz is available for worktrunk extraction (Debian/Ubuntu)  # ← THIS IS THE FAILING TASK
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
    - worktrunk_check.rc != 0
  ansible.builtin.apt:
    name: xz-utils
    state: present
  become: true
  failed_when: false
  # MISSING: tags: [sudo]  ← THE BUG

- name: Install worktrunk from GitHub releases (Debian/Ubuntu, user-level)
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
    - worktrunk_check.rc != 0
    - target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'amd64', 'aarch64', 'arm64']
  block:
    - name: Ensure ~/.local/bin exists (worktrunk)
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin"
        state: directory
        mode: '0755'

    - name: Get latest worktrunk release
      ansible.builtin.uri:
        url: https://api.github.com/repos/max-sixty/worktrunk/releases/latest
        return_content: true
      register: worktrunk_release

    - name: Set worktrunk architecture mapping
      ansible.builtin.set_fact:
        worktrunk_arch: >-
          {{
            'x86_64' if target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'amd64']
            else 'aarch64' if target_architecture in ['aarch64', 'arm64']
            else ''
          }}

    - name: Skip worktrunk on unsupported architecture
      when: worktrunk_arch | trim == ''
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg: "worktrunk skipped: no release for {{ target_architecture }}"

    - name: Set worktrunk download URL fact
      ansible.builtin.set_fact:
        worktrunk_download_url: >-
          {{
            (
              worktrunk_release.json.assets
              | selectattr('name', 'equalto', 'worktrunk-' ~ worktrunk_arch ~ '-unknown-linux-musl.tar.xz')
              | map(attribute='browser_download_url')
              | first
            )
            | default('', true)
          }}

    - name: Skip worktrunk if download URL could not be determined
      when: worktrunk_download_url | trim == ''
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg: "worktrunk skipped: could not determine download URL for architecture {{ worktrunk_arch }}"

    - name: Download worktrunk tarball
      ansible.builtin.get_url:
        url: "{{ worktrunk_download_url }}"
        dest: /tmp/worktrunk.tar.xz
        mode: '0644'
        timeout: 120
      retries: 3
      delay: 5

    - name: Create worktrunk temp directory
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: /tmp/worktrunk
        state: directory
        mode: '0755'

    - name: Extract worktrunk
      ansible.builtin.unarchive:
        src: /tmp/worktrunk.tar.xz
        dest: /tmp/worktrunk
        remote_src: true

    - name: Find worktrunk binary
      ansible.builtin.find:
        paths: /tmp/worktrunk
        patterns: wt
        file_type: file
        recurse: true
      register: worktrunk_find

    - name: Fail if worktrunk binary was not found in extracted archive
      when: worktrunk_find.matched | default(0) | int == 0
      ansible.builtin.fail:
        msg: "worktrunk binary 'wt' was not found under /tmp/worktrunk after extraction"

    - name: Install worktrunk to ~/.local/bin
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        src: "{{ worktrunk_find.files[0].path }}"
        dest: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/wt"
        mode: '0755'
        remote_src: true

    - name: Clean up worktrunk temp files
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: "{{ item }}"
        state: absent
      loop:
        - /tmp/worktrunk.tar.xz
        - /tmp/worktrunk

  rescue:
    - name: Warn worktrunk installation failed
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg: "worktrunk installation failed (likely network timeout) - skipping"

    - name: Clean up worktrunk temp files after failure
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: "{{ item }}"
        state: absent
      loop:
        - /tmp/worktrunk.tar.xz
        - /tmp/worktrunk
```

### 3. HOW NOROOT MODE IS PLUMBED THROUGH THE SYSTEM

**Variable name in Ansible:** The variable is **NOT** automatically passed to Ansible by default. Instead, noRoot mode is handled at the shell script level via `--skip-tags sudo`.

**Chezmoi config definition** (`.chezmoi.toml.tmpl:58`):
```toml
noRoot = {{ promptBoolOnce . "noRoot" "No sudo/root access - skip all system package installations" false }}
```

**Bash script handling** (`run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl`):
- **Line 62:** Determines if ANY sudo is needed:
  ```bash
  NEED_SUDO={{ if or (and (eq .chezmoi.os "linux") (not .noRoot)) (and (eq .chezmoi.os "darwin") .installInputMethod) }}1{{ else }}0{{ end }}
  ```
  
- **Lines 233–268:** When `noRoot=true` on Linux:
  ```bash
  {{ if $noRoot -}}
  # noRoot mode: skip all sudo-requiring tasks, user-level fallbacks will install tools
  info "noRoot mode enabled - installing user-level tools to ~/.local/bin"
  info ""
  info "The following tools will be installed without sudo:"
  ...
  BECOME_FLAGS="--skip-tags sudo"
  ```

This `--skip-tags sudo` flag is passed to the ansible-playbook command (line 333):
```bash
ansible-playbook -i "$INVENTORY" "$PLAYBOOK" --tags "$TAGS" $BECOME_FLAGS ...
```

### 4. PATTERN EXAMPLES — EXISTING TASKS THAT CORRECTLY USE `tags: [sudo]`

**Example 1: jnv xz-utils (same problem, correctly fixed)**  
File: `/home/ldw/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml:3115–3124`

- name: Ensure xz-utils is available for jnv tarball extraction
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
    - jnv_recheck.rc != 0
  become: true
  tags: [sudo]  # ← CORRECT: has the tag
  ansible.builtin.apt:
    name: xz-utils
    state: present
  failed_when: false
```

  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
  become: true
  tags: [sudo]
  ansible.builtin.apt:
    name: bat

```

**Example 3: bats APT install**

```yaml
- name: Install bats (Debian/Ubuntu)
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
  become: true
  tags: [sudo]
  ansible.builtin.apt:
    name: bats-core
    state: present
```

### 5. LINUXBREW CONDITIONAL PATTERN

Linuxbrew is conditionally available and used as a user-level package manager fallback for tools that don't ship musl binaries or have other glibc incompatibilities. The pattern is established in the `television` installation block (lines 2625–2658):

```yaml
- name: Probe for Linuxbrew availability (Debian/Ubuntu, television)
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
    - tv_check.rc != 0
    - target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'amd64', 'aarch64', 'arm64']
  ansible.builtin.shell: command -v brew || true
  args:
    executable: /bin/bash
  register: tv_brew_probe
  changed_when: false

- name: Install television via Linuxbrew (Debian/Ubuntu, brew available)
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
    - tv_check.rc != 0
    - target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'amd64', 'aarch64', 'arm64']
    - tv_brew_probe is defined
    - tv_brew_probe.stdout | default('') | trim != ''
  community.general.homebrew:
    name: television
    state: present
```

The `run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl` (lines 72–77) ensures Linuxbrew is in PATH during ansible execution:
```bash
# Linuxbrew
if [[ -d /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew ]]; then
    eval "$(/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/brew shellenv)"
elif [[ -d "$HOME/.linuxbrew" ]]; then
    eval "$("$HOME/.linuxbrew/bin/brew" shellenv)"
fi
```

### 6. WORKAROUND OPTIONS

**Option A (Recommended):** Add `tags: [sudo]` to the "Ensure xz is available" task (line 2415). This matches the pattern used by jnv on line 3120 and will skip the task in noRoot mode.

**Option B:** Check if worktrunk publishes a `.tar.gz` variant (like sesh does, line 2327). Looking at the selectattr on line 2463, worktrunk currently publishes only `.tar.xz` format:
```
selectattr('name', 'equalto', 'worktrunk-' ~ worktrunk_arch ~ '-unknown-linux-musl.tar.xz')
```

Unlike sesh which publishes `.tar.gz` files (requires no xz), worktrunk does not have a gzip alternative publicly available.

**Option C:** Add a Linuxbrew fallback for xz installation in noRoot mode (similar to the television pattern above). This would:
1. Probe for `brew` availability
2. If available, run `brew install xz`
3. If not available, warn and skip worktrunk installation in noRoot mode

### 7. SUMMARY

| Item | Finding |
|------|---------|
| **Failing task** | Line 2415: "Ensure xz is available for worktrunk extraction" |
| **Root cause** | Missing `tags: [sudo]` annotation |
| **Current behavior** | Executes with `become: true` even in noRoot mode (since --skip-tags sudo doesn't skip it) |
| **Correct variable name** | `--skip-tags sudo` flag passed to ansible-playbook (not an Ansible variable) |

229	- name: Check if tree-sitter is installed
230	  # Search standard PATH dirs INCLUDING ~/.cargo/bin (cargo install target)
231	  # so re-applies don't reinstall on hosts that fell through to the cargo
232	  # fallback path. ansible.builtin.command doesn't honour ~ expansion in
233	  # PATH; use shell with explicit ${HOME}.
234	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
235	  ansible.builtin.shell: |
236	    PATH="${HOME}/.cargo/bin:${PATH}" tree-sitter --version
237	  args:
238	    executable: /bin/bash
239	  register: treesitter_check
240	  changed_when: false
241	  failed_when: false
242	
243	- name: Skip tree-sitter-cli on armv7l (no working node and cargo build too slow)
244	  when:
245	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
246	    - treesitter_check.rc != 0
247	    - target_architecture in ['armv7l', 'armv6l']
248	  ansible.builtin.debug:
249	    msg: "tree-sitter-cli skipped on {{ target_architecture }}: no armv7l node prebuilt; cargo build needs libclang and takes 15+ min"
250	
251	- name: Install tree-sitter-cli via mise npm (Debian/Ubuntu)
252	  # The npm tarball comes from npmmirror (when useChineseMirror=true), but the
253	  # postinstall script `node install.js` ALWAYS downloads a prebuilt binary
254	  # from `https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter/releases/download/...`
255	  # which redirects to release-assets.githubusercontent.com (Azure blob CDN).
256	  # That CDN is frequently unreachable / extremely slow from China, and
257	  # tree-sitter's install.js has no env-var override for the download URL.
258	  # Without an outer timeout the whole `chezmoi apply` hangs indefinitely.
259	  #
260	  # `timeout 180` exits 124 on timeout → treesitter_npm.rc != 0 → cargo
261	  # fallback fires (cargo crates.io is mirrored via TUNA when
262	  # useChineseMirror=true, so cargo path is reliable behind GFW). 180s is
263	  # enough for a working network (full install ~30s) but bounded enough not
264	  # to burn the fleet-apply outer budget.
265	  when:
266	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
267	    - treesitter_check.rc != 0
268	    - target_architecture not in ['armv7l', 'armv6l']
269	  ansible.builtin.shell: |
270	    timeout 180 {{ mise_bin }} exec -- npm install -g tree-sitter-cli
271	  args:
272	    executable: /bin/bash
273	  register: treesitter_npm
274	  changed_when: "'added' in treesitter_npm.stdout or 'added' in treesitter_npm.stderr"
275	  failed_when: false  # Don't fail the play; downstream cargo task handles it.
276	
277	# cargo build of tree-sitter-cli requires libclang (via bindgen). Install on
278	# Debian/Ubuntu when we might fall through to the cargo path.
279	- name: Install libclang-dev for tree-sitter-cli cargo build (Debian/Ubuntu)
280	  # rc != 0 covers both: regular npm failure AND `timeout` exit 124.
281	  # `is failed` alone wouldn't catch rc=124 because failed_when: false above.
282	  when:
283	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
284	    - treesitter_check.rc != 0
285	    - target_architecture not in ['armv7l', 'armv6l']
286	    - treesitter_npm.rc | default(1) != 0
287	  become: true
288	  tags: [sudo]
289	  ansible.builtin.apt:
290	    name: libclang-dev
291	    state: present
292	  ignore_errors: true
293	
294	- name: Install tree-sitter-cli via cargo (fallback)
295	  # Triggered when npm install times out or fails. Cargo pulls from
296	  # crates.io which is TUNA-mirrored when useChineseMirror=true (via
297	  # ~/.cargo/config.toml sparse index), so this path works behind GFW.
298	  when:
299	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
300	    - treesitter_check.rc != 0
301	    - target_architecture not in ['armv7l', 'armv6l']
302	    - treesitter_npm.rc | default(1) != 0
303	  ansible.builtin.shell: |
304	    if command -v cargo >/dev/null 2>&1; then
305	      cargo install tree-sitter-cli
306	    else
307	      echo "Neither Node.js nor cargo available for tree-sitter-cli"
308	      echo "Install manually: cargo install tree-sitter-cli"
309	      exit 0
310	    fi
311	  args:
312	    executable: /bin/bash
313	  changed_when: true
314	  ignore_errors: true

1	# Dotfiles Repository — Agent Contract
2	
3	Cross-platform dotfiles managed by **chezmoi** (configs) + **ansible** (system deps). This file is the agent-facing contract: maintenance rules, hard invariants, and pointers to docs. User-facing intro is in [README.md](README.md).
4	
5	> **Headroom rule**: keep this file under ~30k chars. Push handbook content into `docs/`; keep only edit rules and cross-file invariants here.
6	
7	## Cross-file maintenance rules
8	
9	When you change one of these surfaces, update the listed mirror file in the same commit. These are the rules most often forgotten.
10	
11	### README.md
12	
13	When adding/modifying configurations, update [README.md](README.md):
14	
15	- **New config files** → "What You Get > Config Files" section
16	- **New ansible roles/tools** → "What You Get > Tools" section
17	- **New platforms** → "Supported Platforms" table
18	- **Changed setup steps** → "Quick Setup" section
19	
20	Keep README.md concise and user-focused. Technical details belong here or in `docs/`.
21	
22	### Custom aliases & shell functions → `docs/zsh/aliases.md`
23	
24	When adding/modifying/removing a custom alias or shell function in any `dot_config/zsh/` file, update [`docs/zsh/aliases.md`](docs/zsh/aliases.md): one row per entry with command name, type (`alias` or `function`), source file (relative to repo root), and a one-line description.
25	
26	### Dockerfile
27	
28	When adding new chezmoi prompts in `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl`, also update `Dockerfile`:
29	
30	1. Add corresponding `ARG CHEZMOI_*` build argument.
31	2. Add `--promptBool` or `--promptString` flag to the `chezmoi init` command.
32	
33	This keeps Docker testing in sync with all configuration options.
34	
35	### Agent artifact redaction
36	
37	SpecStory transcripts and coding-agent plan files commonly paste shell output, config snippets, or `.env` values that may contain secrets. Four directories are auto-scanned/redacted:
38	
39	| Prefix | Source |
40	|--------|--------|
41	| `.specstory/history/` | SpecStory chat transcripts |
42	| `.claude/plans/` | Claude Code plan files |
43	| `.cursor/plans/` | Cursor plan files |
44	| `.opencode/plans/` | OpenCode plan files |
45	
46	Tooling: `scripts/redact_secrets.py` (gitleaks + `PRIV***KEY` pattern), `just check-secrets` / `just redact-secrets` / `just add-and-redact`. Pre-commit hook `redact-agent-secrets` runs `--fix` before `gitleaks-system`; if it rewrites a file, stage and retry.
47	
48	When introducing a new coding-agent artifact directory that could contain secrets, add its prefix to `DEFAULT_PATHS` in `scripts/redact_secrets.py` **and** the `files:` regex of the `redact-agent-secrets` pre-commit hook.
49	
50	### Keyboard shortcuts (cross-tool conflict check)
51	
52	When adding/modifying keybindings in any tool config, cross-check against other tools — multiple tools share the terminal's key namespace, especially `Ctrl+` and `Alt+`.
53	
54	| Tool | Config file | Conflict risk |
55	|------|-------------|---------------|
56	| tmux (root-table) | `dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf` | `C-h/j/k/l` (vim-tmux-navigator), `C-1..9` (window switch) |
57	| Television (global) | `dot_config/television/config.toml` | `Ctrl+S/F/R/Y/T/X/O` (built-in actions) |
58	| Television (channels) | `dot_config/television/cable/*.toml` | Per-channel `[keybindings]` overrides global |
59	| Zellij | `dot_config/zellij/config.kdl` | Mitigated by `default_mode "locked"` |
60	| Ghostty | `dot_config/ghostty/config` | `macos-option-as-alt` affects `Alt+` availability |
61	
62	Known conflict zones: `Ctrl+H/J/K/L` (tmux vim-tmux-navigator; removed in TV global), `Ctrl+S/F/R` (TV built-in cycling/reload — avoid in channel actions), `Alt+*` (safe namespace for channel-specific actions; requires terminal to send Option as Meta).
63	
64	**Resolution precedence**: tmux root-table bindings intercept keys before they reach the inner application. Inside tmux, any `bind-key -n C-*` shadows the same `ctrl-*` in TV. Prefer `Alt+` for custom actions.

93	### fleet-apply (`scripts/fleet_apply.py` + `dot_config/fleet/`)
94	
95	Touching any of these surfaces requires updating [`docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`](docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md) in the same commit:
96	
97	- `scripts/fleet_apply.py` — CLI flags, mode semantics, sudo helper integration, log/sentinel paths
98	- `justfile` `fleet-*` recipes — name, args, doc-comment
99	- `dot_config/fleet/create_private_machines.toml.tmpl` — schema (`local`, `chezmoi_path`, `no_root_machine`, `password.source`, etc.)
100	- Any change to `scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh` that affects how `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` is consumed (also see "Sudo session" invariant below)
101	
102	`README.md` only needs an update if the user-facing `## Multi-host apply` block changes (top-level recipe names, exit-code semantics).
103	
104	## Chezmoi templating conventions
105	
106	**Hard rule**: before adding a `{{ if eq .profile ... }}` branch, ask if the predicate is auto-detectable. If yes, use `.chezmoi.os` / `.chezmoi.arch` / `.chezmoi.hostname` instead. `.profile` exists only for user-role choices chezmoi cannot infer (server vs desktop).
107	
108	| Predicate | Use |
109	|---|---|
110	| Any macOS (Apple Silicon or Intel) | `eq .chezmoi.os "darwin"` |
111	| Any Linux | `eq .chezmoi.os "linux"` |
112	| Apple Silicon only | `eq .chezmoi.arch "arm64"` (inside darwin-scoped files) or `and (eq .chezmoi.os "darwin") (eq .chezmoi.arch "arm64")` |
113	| Intel Mac only | `and (eq .chezmoi.os "darwin") (eq .chezmoi.arch "amd64")` |
114	| Desktop vs headless (user role) | `.profile` — `ubuntu_desktop` / `ubuntu_server`; macOS side covered by `eq .chezmoi.os "darwin"` |
115	
116	Profile values are intentionally limited to `macos`, `ubuntu_desktop`, `ubuntu_server`. **Do not** introduce new profile values for OS/arch facts (the historical `macos_intel` profile was removed for exactly this reason).
117	
118	Full decision table, before/after examples, and the `macos_intel` migration snippet: [docs/tools/chezmoi-templating.md](docs/tools/chezmoi-templating.md).
119	
120	## Hard repo invariants
121	
122	### Install vs upgrade is split on purpose
123	
124	`chezmoi apply` (+ ansible phase) is deliberately **install-only**: roles use `state: present` / `creates:` so re-applying never silently bumps every tool. The explicit upgrade path lives in [`scripts/upgrade_tools.sh`](scripts/upgrade_tools.sh), exposed via `just upgrade-*` recipes.
125	
126	- **Do not** rewrite ansible roles to `state: latest`.
127	- **Do not** add `apt upgrade` / system package bumps to default scope.
128	- `scripts/**` is in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`, so `upgrade_tools.sh` is never deployed; it runs from the repo directly.
129	- Adding a new upgrade category: see [docs/this_repo/upgrades.md](docs/this_repo/upgrades.md) → "Adding a new category". For a tool already managed by an existing package manager (brew/uv/npm/cargo/dotnet/gem/mise) you do nothing — generic `upgrade` picks it up.
130	
131	Full per-category matrix, sample output, and troubleshooting: [docs/this_repo/upgrades.md](docs/this_repo/upgrades.md). The short version is also mirrored in `README.md`.
132	
133	### Sudo session is shared across all run-scripts
134	
135	All three `run_*` scripts share one sudo session via `scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh`. The user is prompted **once** at the start of `chezmoi apply` and downstream scripts reuse the cached credential silently.
136	
137	**Hard rules** when touching run-scripts:
138	
139	- Do **not** re-implement `sudo -k` / `sudo -v` / TTY-read logic. Call the shared helper.
140	- Do **not** run `sudo -k` (invalidates the shared cache for the whole flow).
141	- Do **not** register a `trap … EXIT` that removes state (next run-script needs it).
142	- Do **not** read the password into a shell variable. Always pipe via `sudo -S <file`.
143	
144	Adding a new sudo surface in a run-script:
145	
146	1. `{{ include "scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh" }}` near the top of the template.
147	2. Set the `NEED_SUDO` template flag (mirror existing run-scripts).
148	3. Call `sudo_session_init "yourlabel"`; branch on return code + `sudo_session_skip_reason`.
149	4. Run privileged commands via `sudo_run …` (simple cases) or pass `-e @$CHEZMOI_ANSIBLE_BECOME_FILE` to ansible.
150	
151	Full helper API, runtime state, cleanup model: [docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md](docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md).
152	
153	**Non-interactive password injection** (used by `scripts/fleet_apply.py` over
154	SSH): `sudo_session_init` adopts `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` (a 0600 file
155	path) instead of prompting on `/dev/tty`. The helper validates with `sudo -S
156	-v -p ''` and writes into the same shared state dir, so downstream
157	run-scripts see the cached state and never re-prompt. Do **not** read
158	`CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` from your run-script directly — always go
159	through `sudo_session_init`. See [docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md](docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md)
160	→ "Non-interactive password injection" and [docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md](docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md)
161	for the orchestrator side.
162	
163	### fleet-apply semantics (counter-intuitive defaults)
164	
165	A few `just fleet-apply*` behaviours WILL trip up agents who don't know them. Full docs in [`docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`](docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md); the load-bearing invariants:
166	
167	- **`drift` ≠ `failed`**. When chezmoi can't prompt to overwrite a hand-edited file (no PTY over SSH), the host is shown as yellow ⚠ `drift` in the live table and the per-file paths are listed, but it does **not** count toward the exit code. Don't "fix" drift hosts unless the user asks. Resolution: hand-fix the remote, or `--force` to let the template win.
168	- **`fleet-apply-file PATH` skips `run_*` scripts**. Uses `chezmoi apply --exclude=scripts <PATH>` after an explicit `git pull`. Means ansible / Brewfile changes will NOT execute. If you edit `dot_ansible/...` and test with `fleet-apply-file`, the change won't apply — use full `fleet-apply` for ansible iterations. Same applies to Brewfile.
169	- **`--branch BRANCH` is no-op on local hosts**. The local source dir IS the user's editor working tree; switching it would be hostile. Local hosts log a warning and run against the working tree as-is. The flag also forces mode to `apply` (since `chezmoi update` would re-pull main and undo the checkout).
170	- **Install-only by design**. fleet-apply inherits the [Install vs upgrade is split](#install-vs-upgrade-is-split-on-purpose) invariant: it never silently bumps tools. The explicit upgrade path is `just upgrade-*` which must be run on each host (fleet-apply does NOT broadcast upgrades).
171	- **Process substitution + sentinel are load-bearing**. `> >(tee -a $log) 2>&1 & _cz_pid=$!; wait $_cz_pid; _rc=$?; echo $_rc > $sentinel` is the contract that `--status` / `--tail` / `--watch` rely on. Don't change to a pipeline (`| tee`) — the wrapper's SIGHUP trap depends on `$_cz_pid` pointing to chezmoi, not tee. See [docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md → Killing orphans, checking status, re-attaching](docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md#killing-orphans-checking-status-re-attaching).
172	- **Conservative drift classifier**. `_classify_drift()` only downgrades stderr lines matching the exact `chezmoi: <path>: could not open a new TTY: open /dev/tty:` fingerprint. Any unrecognised stderr line keeps `failed` state. Don't broaden the regex without explicit user request — silent downgrades hide real errors.
173	
174	### `modify_` and `create_` prefix semantics
175	
176	Two chezmoi source prefixes tame files that would otherwise churn on every apply:
177	
178	- **`modify_`** files are executable scripts: chezmoi pipes current target contents into stdin, expects new contents on stdout. Used for `~/.claude/settings.json` (jq overlay), the editor `settings.json` files (VSCode/Cursor/Antigravity), and the coding-agent CLI configs (`~/.cursor/cli-config.json`, `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`, `~/.codex/config.toml`). Do **not** `chezmoi add` a `modify_` target — it would overwrite your script with the live file.
179	- **`create_`** files seed once, then chezmoi never touches the contents. Used for `~/.config/nvim/lazy-lock.json` and editor `keybindings.json`. To refresh a `create_` baseline, copy the live file directly into the source path: `cp <target> "$(chezmoi source-path <target>)"`. Neither `chezmoi add` (strips the prefix) nor `chezmoi re-add` (silently skips) is correct.
180	
181	Full case studies (`dot_claude/modify_settings.json`, `.chezmoitemplates/editor/*`, `dot_config/nvim/create_lazy-lock.json`, `dot_codex/modify_config.toml`), failure modes, presence-gating in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`: [docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md → Case studies in this repo](docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md#case-studies-in-this-repo). For the three coding-agent CLI overlays specifically, the deep-dive lives at [docs/tools/agent-overlays.md](docs/tools/agent-overlays.md) (overlay key rationale, what's intentionally NOT managed and why, OpenCode legacy `config.json` migration, Codex `[projects]`/`[marketplaces.*]` round-trip, **and the Claude hook-aware merger that lets our overlay coexist with [CodeIsland](https://github.com/wxtsky/CodeIsland)'s auto-installed hook entries on macOS** without ping-ponging on every apply).
182	
183	### Tmux ≥ 3.3 required for popup menu, and menu must fit terminal height
184	
185	The popup menu is bound to **both** `prefix + Space` and `prefix + e` (alias) and is **generated by `~/.config/tmux/menu.sh`**, not defined inline in `keybindings.conf`. Two unrelated tmux quirks force this:
186	
187	1. **Position clamping (tmux ≥ 3.3 required)**: `display-menu -x R -y P` places the menu past the terminal edge on tmux 3.2a (Ubuntu 22.04 apt) and silently suppresses it. tmux 3.3+ clamps the position. The Ansible `devtools` role detects old tmux on Debian/Ubuntu and upgrades automatically (Linuxbrew when present, otherwise user-level [`nelsonenzo/tmux-appimage`](https://github.com/nelsonenzo/tmux-appimage) extracted to `~/.local/share/tmux-appimage/` with a shim at `~/.local/bin/tmux`). After the upgrade, run `tmux kill-server` once — running servers keep the old binary in memory.
188	2. **Menu-too-tall silent failure (all tmux versions)**: `display-menu` does **not** paginate. If the menu is taller than the terminal (after status bar + `-y` anchor offset), the entire popup is suppressed with no error, no log entry, nothing in `tmux show-messages`. `man tmux`: _"If the menu is too large to fit on the terminal, it is not displayed."_ This was misdiagnosed for hours as a `csi-u` / `extended-keys` keysym encoding bug after a 50-row flat menu started failing on smaller terminal heights — the keys (`Space` then `Enter` then `e`) were all bound correctly the whole time.
189	
190	Hard rules when touching the popup menu:
191	
192	- **Top menu cap is ~14 rows.** Adding a 15th row will start failing on smaller heights (mobile SSH, half-screen splits). Push lower-frequency items into the appropriate submenu in `~/.config/tmux/menu-<category>.sh` instead.
193	- **Submenus are separate scripts**, each `exec tmux display-menu …`. Quoting context resets per script — keeps the inline `\"` / `{` / `}` / `;` quoting disasters out of `keybindings.conf`.
194	- **Complex commands** (anything with `{`, `}`, `;`, backticks, or nested fzf binds) must live in their own script (`~/.config/tmux/sesh-picker.sh`, `sesh-windows.sh`, etc.), not inline in a menu row. tmux's parser treats `{` `}` `;` as command-block delimiters / separators even inside `'…'` inside `"…"`, silently aborting parse.
195	- **Test by shrinking the terminal vertically.** Verifying on a full-height window does not catch the height-fit failure. The top menu generator reads `#{client_height}` and tier-trims; if you change the tiers, retest at heights 14 / 22 / 60.
196	
197	See `pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md` for the full debugging story (red herrings included). Adjacent pitfall: `pitfalls/yazi-tmux-popup-crash.md`.
198	
199	### Key tmux settings for coding agents
200	
201	These are non-obvious settings that other tools depend on; do not remove without checking:
202	
203	- `extended-keys always` + `terminal-features 'xterm*:extkeys'` — forwards Shift+Enter, Ctrl+Enter through tmux to inner apps (Claude Code, Neovim, etc.)
204	- `escape-time 0` — eliminates ESC delay for Neovim
205	- `set-clipboard on` + `terminal-features …:clipboard` (for `xterm*`, `ghostty*`, `alacritty*`) — OSC 52 over SSH without terminfo `Ms`. Paired with SSH-conditional `vim.g.clipboard = vim.ui.clipboard.osc52` in `dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua`. See [docs/tools/tmux/README.md](docs/tools/tmux/README.md) → "OSC 52 Clipboard".
206	- `allow-passthrough on` — OSC passthrough for terminal images
207	- macOS terminals must send Option as Meta/Esc+ for `M-` keybindings (theme switching, layouts, fine resize). Ghostty/cmux: `macos-option-as-alt = left` (managed in `dot_config/ghostty/config`). See [docs/tools/ghostty.md](docs/tools/ghostty.md).
208	
209	Full tmux config breakdown, theme switching, keybindings table, troubleshooting: [docs/tools/tmux/](docs/tools/tmux/).
210	
211	### Zellij `default_mode "locked"`
212	
213	`dot_config/zellij/config.kdl` uses `default_mode "locked"` so all keys pass through to inner applications by default. Press `Ctrl+G` to unlock Zellij commands. This prevents key conflicts with coding agents and vim-style applications. On first Zellij launch (without existing config), select the "Unlock-First (non-colliding)" keybinding preset.
214

// Determine the URL of the file.
const platform = matrix.platform[process.platform];
const arch = platform?.arch[process.arch];

if (!platform || !platform.name || !arch || !arch.name) {
  console.error(
    `Cannot install tree-sitter-cli for platform ${process.platform}, architecture ${process.arch}`
  );
  process.exit(1);
}

const releaseURL = `https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter/releases/download/v${packageJSON.version}`;
const assetName = `tree-sitter-${platform.name}-${arch.name}.gz`;
const assetURL = `${releaseURL}/${assetName}`;

// Remove previously-downloaded files.
const executableName = process.platform === 'win32' ? 'tree-sitter.exe' : 'tree-sitter';
if (fs.existsSync(executableName)) {
  fs.unlinkSync(executableName);
}

// Download the compressed file.
console.log(`Downloading ${assetURL}`);
const file = fs.createWriteStream(executableName);
get(assetURL, response => {
  if (response.statusCode > 299) {
    console.error([
      'Download failed',
      '',
      `url: ${assetURL}`,
      `status: ${response.statusCode}`,
      `headers: ${JSON.stringify(response.headers, null, 2)}`,
      '',
    ].join('\n'));
    process.exit(1);
  }
  response.pipe(zlib.createGunzip()).pipe(file);
});

file.on('finish', () => {
  fs.chmodSync(executableName, '755');
});

// Follow redirects.
function get(url, callback) {
  const processResponse = (response) => {
    if (response.statusCode === 301 || response.statusCode === 302) {
      get(response.headers.location, callback);
    } else {
      callback(response);
    }
  };

  const proxyEnv = process.env.HTTPS_PROXY || process.env.https_proxy;
  if (!proxyEnv) {
    https.get(url, processResponse);
    return;
  }

  const requestUrl = new URL(url);
  const requestPort = requestUrl.port || (requestUrl.protocol === 'https:' ? 443 : 80);
  const proxyUrl = new URL(proxyEnv);
  const request = proxyUrl.protocol === 'https:' ? https : http;
  const requestOption = {
    host: proxyUrl.hostname,
    port: proxyUrl.port || (proxyUrl.protocol === 'https:' ? 443 : 80),
    method: 'CONNECT',
    path: `${requestUrl.hostname}:${requestPort}`,
  };
  if (proxyUrl.username || proxyUrl.password) {
    const auth = `${decodeURIComponent(
      proxyUrl.username
    )}:${decodeURIComponent(proxyUrl.password)}`;
    requestOption.headers = {
      'Proxy-Authorization': `Basic ${Buffer.from(
        auth
      ).toString('base64')}`,
    }
  }
  request.request(requestOption).on('connect', (response, socket, _head) => {
    if (response.statusCode !== 200) {
      // let caller handle error
      callback(response);
      return;
    }

    const agent = https.Agent({ socket });
    https.get({
      host: requestUrl.host,
      port: requestPort,
      path: `${requestUrl.pathname}${requestUrl.search}`,
      agent,
    }, processResponse);
  }).end();
}

Perfect! I found the problem. Look at this code:

```javascript
file.on('finish', () => {
  fs.chmodSync(executableName, '755');
});
```

The install.js script calls `fs.chmodSync(executableName, '755')` to make the binary executable **after** the file write finishes. However, this chmod happens **asynchronously** relative to the file write completion. The file is empty because the download **failed** but the script didn't exit - it just created an empty file.

Also, notice that the chmod uses a string `'755'` instead of octal `0o755`. Let me verify this is actually the issue and check the error handling:

Looking at the install.js more carefully:
1. A stream is created: `fs.createWriteStream(executableName)`
2. If the response status is > 299, it tries to exit... but the file is already being written
3. The response gets piped through gunzip into the file
4. When the file finishes writing, it chmodods to '755'

The problem is: **the `file.on('finish')` event handler might not be catching errors from the decompression stream**. A failed download from the CDN (GitHub release assets hosted on Azure) would result in an empty file with incorrect permissions.

## Diagnosis Report: tree-sitter Permission Issue

### ROOT CAUSE

The `tree-sitter` binary file at `/home/ldw/.local/share/mise/installs/node/24.13.0/lib/node_modules/tree-sitter-cli/tree-sitter` is **empty (0 bytes)** with **permissions 0600 (rw-------)** instead of the expected executable binary. This occurred when the ansible task `Install mise global tools (Debian/Ubuntu)` ran on 2026-04-22 23:16:25.

### What Happened

1. **Ansible task** (line 270 in `/home/ldw/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ansible/roles/lazyvim_deps/tasks/main.yml`):
   ```yaml
   timeout 180 {{ mise_bin }} exec -- npm install -g tree-sitter-cli
   ```
   This runs `npm install -g tree-sitter-cli` inside the mise node environment.

2. **tree-sitter-cli postinstall** (in `/home/ldw/.local/share/mise/installs/node/24.13.0/lib/node_modules/tree-sitter-cli/package.json`):
   - `"scripts": { "install": "node install.js" }`
   - The `install.js` script attempts to download a prebuilt binary from GitHub releases (redirected via Azure CDN)
   - The download **failed** (likely due to network issues, timeouts, or GFW blocking), creating an empty file
   - The script then calls `fs.chmodSync(executableName, '755')` to make it executable
   - **However**, the string `'755'` in JavaScript gets interpreted as an octal literal in some Node.js versions, but the real issue is the file was already empty before chmod

3. **Why the error occurs**:
   - nvim-treesitter spawns `/home/ldw/.local/share/mise/installs/node/24.13.0/lib/node_modules/tree-sitter-cli/tree-sitter` directly
   - This file is empty and has no execute bit (mode 0600 instead of 0755)
   - Result: `EACCES` (permission denied on spawn)

### Verification of Current State

**File permissions at `/home/ldw/.local/share/mise/installs/node/24.13.0/lib/node_modules/tree-sitter-cli/`:**
```
-rw-------  (0600) tree-sitter          ← EMPTY FILE (0 bytes), created 2026-04-22 23:16
-rwx------ (0700) cli.js                ← #!/usr/bin/env node executable wrapper (CORRECT)
-rw------- (0600) dsl.d.ts
-rw------- (0600) install.js
-rw------- (0600) package.json
```

**Shim at `~/.local/share/mise/shims/tree-sitter`:**
```
lrwxrwxrwx (0755) tree-sitter → /home/ldw/.local/bin/mise  ✓ (CORRECT)
```

**PATH resolution:**
```
which tree-sitter → /home/ldw/.local/share/mise/installs/node/24.13.0/bin/tree-sitter
                     (which is a symlink to ../lib/node_modules/tree-sitter-cli/cli.js ✓)
```

**Mise config** (`/home/ldw/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/mise/config.toml.tmpl`):
```toml
[tools]
node = "lts"      ← Only node is explicitly listed
```
tree-sitter-cli comes in via `npm install -g`, not as a direct mise tool.

### Why the Binary is Empty

The `install.js` postinstall script in tree-sitter-cli attempts to:
1. Download a prebuilt binary from: `https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter/releases/download/v0.26.8/tree-sitter-linux-x64.gz`
2. Decompress it into `./tree-sitter`
3. Make it executable with `fs.chmodSync(executableName, '755')`

**The download failed** (network timeout, Azure CDN unreachable, GFW blocking, etc.), but the empty file was left behind with incorrect permissions. The script doesn't have robust error handling for stream failures — if the gunzip stream fails silently, you get an empty file.

### Minimal Fix

**Option A (Immediate, user-level):** Remove the empty file and let npm reinstall it correctly
```bash
rm /home/ldw/.local/share/mise/installs/node/24.13.0/lib/node_modules/tree-sitter-cli/tree-sitter
npm install -g tree-sitter-cli  # or: mise exec -- npm install -g tree-sitter-cli
```

**Option B (Root-level, ansible):** Add a postinstall check/fix to the ansible task in `/home/ldw/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ansible/roles/lazyvim_deps/tasks/main.yml` (after line 276) to verify the binary is non-empty after npm install, or set a longer timeout.

**Option C (Robust fix for future runs):** The ansible playbook already has fallback logic (lines 294-315) to install tree-sitter-cli via cargo if npm fails. The npm path should either:
- Verify the downloaded binary is not empty before continuing
- Or allow the fallback path to trigger on npm timeout/failure (currently it does, but npm might exit 0 even with empty file)

### No umask Issues

- chezmoi umask is correctly set to `0o022` (files get 0644, dirs 0755)
- No problematic umask directives in `dot_zshrc.tmpl` or `dot_zshenv.tmpl`
- The permission problem is entirely due to the failed download + empty file, not umask

### nvim-treesitter Configuration

No custom treesitter config overrides found in the chezmoi repo. The plugin uses its default behavior of searching for and spawning the `tree-sitter` CLI binary from the PATH or pre-bundled parsers.

## Investigation Report: Worktrunk XZ Installation Issue in noRoot Mode

### 1. ROOT CAUSE
The task at `/home/ldw/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml:2415` is **missing the `tags: [sudo]` annotation**. In noRoot mode, the ansible playbook runs with `--skip-tags sudo` (set in `run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl:249`), which should skip this task. However, since it lacks the tag, it still executes with `become: true`, triggering the `sudo: a password is required` error.

### 2. EXACT YAML BLOCK — WORKTRUNK INSTALL SECTION

**File:** `/home/ldw/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml`  
**Lines:** 2405–2536

  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
  ansible.builtin.command: wt --version
  register: worktrunk_check
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false
  environment:
    PATH: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin:/usr/local/bin:{{ ansible_facts['env']['PATH'] }}"

    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
    - worktrunk_check.rc != 0
  ansible.builtin.apt:
    name: xz-utils
    state: present
  become: true
  failed_when: false
  # MISSING: tags: [sudo]  ← THE BUG

- name: Install worktrunk from GitHub releases (Debian/Ubuntu, user-level)
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
    - worktrunk_check.rc != 0
    - target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'amd64', 'aarch64', 'arm64']
  block:
    - name: Ensure ~/.local/bin exists (worktrunk)
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin"
        state: directory
        mode: '0755'

    - name: Get latest worktrunk release
      ansible.builtin.uri:
        url: https://api.github.com/repos/max-sixty/worktrunk/releases/latest
        return_content: true
      register: worktrunk_release

    - name: Set worktrunk architecture mapping
      ansible.builtin.set_fact:
        worktrunk_arch: >-
          {{
            'x86_64' if target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'amd64']
            else 'aarch64' if target_architecture in ['aarch64', 'arm64']
            else ''
          }}

    - name: Skip worktrunk on unsupported architecture
      when: worktrunk_arch | trim == ''
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg: "worktrunk skipped: no release for {{ target_architecture }}"

    - name: Set worktrunk download URL fact
      ansible.builtin.set_fact:
        worktrunk_download_url: >-
          {{
            (
              worktrunk_release.json.assets
              | selectattr('name', 'equalto', 'worktrunk-' ~ worktrunk_arch ~ '-unknown-linux-musl.tar.xz')
              | map(attribute='browser_download_url')
              | first
            )
            | default('', true)
          }}

    - name: Skip worktrunk if download URL could not be determined
      when: worktrunk_download_url | trim == ''
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg: "worktrunk skipped: could not determine download URL for architecture {{ worktrunk_arch }}"

    - name: Download worktrunk tarball
      ansible.builtin.get_url:
        url: "{{ worktrunk_download_url }}"
        dest: /tmp/worktrunk.tar.xz
        mode: '0644'
        timeout: 120
      retries: 3
      delay: 5

    - name: Create worktrunk temp directory
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: /tmp/worktrunk
        state: directory
        mode: '0755'

    - name: Extract worktrunk
      ansible.builtin.unarchive:
        src: /tmp/worktrunk.tar.xz
        dest: /tmp/worktrunk
        remote_src: true

    - name: Find worktrunk binary
      ansible.builtin.find:
        paths: /tmp/worktrunk
        patterns: wt
        file_type: file
        recurse: true
      register: worktrunk_find

    - name: Fail if worktrunk binary was not found in extracted archive
      when: worktrunk_find.matched | default(0) | int == 0
      ansible.builtin.fail:
        msg: "worktrunk binary 'wt' was not found under /tmp/worktrunk after extraction"

    - name: Install worktrunk to ~/.local/bin

        dest: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/wt"
        mode: '0755'
        remote_src: true

      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: "{{ item }}"
        state: absent

    - name: Clean up worktrunk temp files after failure

        path: "{{ item }}"
        state: absent
      loop:
        - /tmp/worktrunk.tar.xz
        - /tmp/worktrunk

### 3. HOW NOROOT MODE IS PLUMBED THROUGH THE SYSTEM

**Variable name in Ansible:** The variable is **NOT** automatically passed to Ansible by default. Instead, noRoot mode is handled at the shell script level via `--skip-tags sudo`.

**Chezmoi config definition** (`.chezmoi.toml.tmpl:58`):
```toml
noRoot = {{ promptBoolOnce . "noRoot" "No sudo/root access - skip all system package installations" false }}
```

**Bash script handling** (`run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl`):
- **Line 62:** Determines if ANY sudo is needed:
  ```bash
  NEED_SUDO={{ if or (and (eq .chezmoi.os "linux") (not .noRoot)) (and (eq .chezmoi.os "darwin") .installInputMethod) }}1{{ else }}0{{ end }}
  ```
  
- **Lines 233–268:** When `noRoot=true` on Linux:
  ```bash
  {{ if $noRoot -}}
  # noRoot mode: skip all sudo-requiring tasks, user-level fallbacks will install tools
  info "noRoot mode enabled - installing user-level tools to ~/.local/bin"
  info ""
  info "The following tools will be installed without sudo:"
  ...
  BECOME_FLAGS="--skip-tags sudo"
  ```

This `--skip-tags sudo` flag is passed to the ansible-playbook command (line 333):
```bash
ansible-playbook -i "$INVENTORY" "$PLAYBOOK" --tags "$TAGS" $BECOME_FLAGS ...
```

### 5. LINUXBREW CONDITIONAL PATTERN

Linuxbrew is conditionally available and used as a user-level package manager fallback for tools that don't ship musl binaries or have other glibc incompatibilities. The pattern is established in the `television` installation block (lines 2625–2658):

```yaml
- name: Probe for Linuxbrew availability (Debian/Ubuntu, television)
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
    - tv_check.rc != 0
    - target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'amd64', 'aarch64', 'arm64']
  ansible.builtin.shell: command -v brew || true
  args:
    executable: /bin/bash
  register: tv_brew_probe
  changed_when: false

- name: Install television via Linuxbrew (Debian/Ubuntu, brew available)
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
    - tv_check.rc != 0
    - target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'amd64', 'aarch64', 'arm64']
    - tv_brew_probe is defined
    - tv_brew_probe.stdout | default('') | trim != ''
  community.general.homebrew:
    name: television
    state: present
```

The `run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl` (lines 72–77) ensures Linuxbrew is in PATH during ansible execution:
```bash
# Linuxbrew
if [[ -d /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew ]]; then
    eval "$(/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/brew shellenv)"
elif [[ -d "$HOME/.linuxbrew" ]]; then
    eval "$("$HOME/.linuxbrew/bin/brew" shellenv)"
fi
```

### 6. WORKAROUND OPTIONS

**Option A (Recommended):** Add `tags: [sudo]` to the "Ensure xz is available" task (line 2415). This matches the pattern used by jnv on line 3120 and will skip the task in noRoot mode.

**Option B:** Check if worktrunk publishes a `.tar.gz` variant (like sesh does, line 2327). Looking at the selectattr on line 2463, worktrunk currently publishes only `.tar.xz` format:
```
selectattr('name', 'equalto', 'worktrunk-' ~ worktrunk_arch ~ '-unknown-linux-musl.tar.xz')
```

Unlike sesh which publishes `.tar.gz` files (requires no xz), worktrunk does not have a gzip alternative publicly available.

**Option C:** Add a Linuxbrew fallback for xz installation in noRoot mode (similar to the television pattern above). This would:
1. Probe for `brew` availability
2. If available, run `brew install xz`
3. If not available, warn and skip worktrunk installation in noRoot mode

### 7. SUMMARY

| Item | Finding |
|------|---------|
| **Failing task** | Line 2415: "Ensure xz is available for worktrunk extraction" |
| **Root cause** | Missing `tags: [sudo]` annotation |
| **Current behavior** | Executes with `become: true` even in noRoot mode (since --skip-tags sudo doesn't skip it) |
| **Correct variable name** | `--skip-tags sudo` flag passed to ansible-playbook (not an Ansible variable) |
| **Pattern examples** | Lines 3120 (jnv), 97 (gh), 241 (bat), 353 (bats) all have `tags: [sudo]` |
| **Linuxbrew available?** | Yes, conditionally enabled (checked in run_onchange script) and used by television/taplo installations |
| **User-level xz fallback?** | Linuxbrew can provide `xz`, but worktrunk publishes only `.tar.xz` not `.tar.gz` |

# `chezmoi apply` on jingle-207 (noRoot=true): two bugs

## Context

On `jingle-207` (Ubuntu 22.04, ubuntu_server profile, **noRoot=true**), `chezmoi apply` fails with two independent issues:

1. **ansible task hits `sudo: a password is required`** at `devtools : Ensure xz is available for worktrunk extraction (Debian/Ubuntu)` even though the machine is in noRoot mode. Root cause: that task is missing the `tags: [sudo]` annotation, so `ansible-playbook --skip-tags sudo` (the mechanism this repo uses to honor noRoot) doesn't skip it. Exit status 2 from `run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh` aborts the whole `chezmoi apply`.

2. **Neovim `nvim-treesitter` parser builds fail with `EACCES`** on every language. The native tree-sitter binary at `/home/ldw/.local/share/mise/installs/node/24.13.0/lib/node_modules/tree-sitter-cli/tree-sitter` is a **0-byte file with mode `0600`** (neither executable nor has any content). Caused by an earlier `npm install -g tree-sitter-cli` whose postinstall `install.js` download stream silently failed (GitHub release CDN → Azure blob is flaky behind GFW), leaving the empty file behind. Ansible's detection is too weak to notice: `treesitter_check` runs `tree-sitter --version`, which in `cli.js` just reads `package.json` — it exits `0` reporting `0.26.8` without ever touching the broken native binary. So every re-apply happily skips the reinstall.

Both are broad "install path is too optimistic about success / too naive about capability" bugs, so the fix for each is a small guard in the same ansible role.

## Bug 1: worktrunk xz task missing `tags: [sudo]` (+ wasted work in noRoot)

### Current state

`dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml:2415–2423`:

\```yaml
- name: Ensure xz is available for worktrunk extraction (Debian/Ubuntu)
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
    - worktrunk_check.rc != 0
  ansible.builtin.apt:
    name: xz-utils
    state: present
  become: true
  failed_when: false
  # ← missing tags: [sudo]
\```

Precedent for the fix already exists in the same file — `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml:3115` (`Ensure xz-utils is available for jnv tarball extraction`) does it correctly, and the noRoot plumbing (`BECOME_FLAGS="--skip-tags sudo"`) is in `run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl:249`.

### Downstream consequence in noRoot mode

Even after tagging, the rest of the worktrunk block (lines 2425–2522) will still run and attempt `get_url` + `unarchive` on a `.tar.xz`. If `xz` isn't already on PATH (linuxbrew etc.), extraction fails, the `rescue:` block warns and cleans up. That's correct graceful degradation, but **wastes a ~4MB download + 2 retries on every apply** on every noRoot machine without xz. Worktrunk only publishes `-musl.tar.xz` — no `.tar.gz` alternative — confirmed via live `gh api`.

### Fix

Two-part change to `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml`:

**(a) Tag the apt task so `--skip-tags sudo` honors it** (line 2415):

\```yaml
- name: Ensure xz is available for worktrunk extraction (Debian/Ubuntu)
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
    - worktrunk_check.rc != 0
  become: true
  tags: [sudo]          # ← add this
  ansible.builtin.apt:
    name: xz-utils
    state: present
  failed_when: false
\```

**(b) Probe for `xz` after the apt task and gate the install block on it** — insert between the apt task and the existing `Install worktrunk from GitHub releases …` block (before line 2425):

\```yaml
- name: Probe for xz binary (worktrunk extraction dependency)
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
    - worktrunk_check.rc != 0
  ansible.builtin.shell: command -v xz || true
  args:
    executable: /bin/bash
  register: worktrunk_xz_probe
  changed_when: false
\```

Then extend the `when:` of the install block (currently 2427–2429) with one more condition:

\```yaml
- name: Install worktrunk from GitHub releases (Debian/Ubuntu, user-level)
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
    - worktrunk_check.rc != 0
    - target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'amd64', 'aarch64', 'arm64']
    - worktrunk_xz_probe.stdout | default('') | trim != ''     # ← add this
  block:
    …
\```

Result: on noRoot machines without xz, the apt task is skipped (tagged), the probe finds no xz, the block is skipped entirely with no wasted download/retries. On rooted or brew-equipped machines xz is present and the block runs as before. This matches the existing `television` / `taplo` pattern (probe linuxbrew, branch on presence) already in this file.

## Bug 2: tree-sitter detection can't see an empty native binary

### Current state

`dot_ansible/roles/lazyvim_deps/tasks/main.yml:229–241`:

\```yaml
- name: Check if tree-sitter is installed
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
  ansible.builtin.shell: |
    PATH="${HOME}/.cargo/bin:${PATH}" tree-sitter --version
  args: { executable: /bin/bash }
  register: treesitter_check
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false
\```

Verified locally: `tree-sitter --version` returns `tree-sitter 0.26.8` with **rc=0** despite the native binary being 0 bytes. `cli.js` returns the version from `package.json`, never spawning the native binary. So the npm+cargo reinstall paths at lines 251 / 294 are never reached on a broken-empty-binary host.

The 0-byte binary itself comes from an upstream bug in `tree-sitter-cli`'s `install.js`: a failed download leaves an empty destination file, and the process still exits 0. We can't fix that from here — we have to detect it.

### Fix

Strengthen `treesitter_check` to also probe a parse-path code path that requires the native binary. The cheapest proxy: generate a tiny grammar or run `tree-sitter dump-languages` / `tree-sitter parse` — but those are overkill and add dependencies.

Simpler: split the check into two registers. First `--version` (cheap sanity), then — only if `--version` succeeded — a second probe that **verifies the resolved `tree-sitter` binary at the end of symlink chain is a non-empty executable**. Keep `failed_when: false` on both.

New block replacing lines 229–241:

\```yaml
- name: Check if tree-sitter --version works
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
  ansible.builtin.shell: |
    PATH="${HOME}/.cargo/bin:${PATH}" tree-sitter --version
  args: { executable: /bin/bash }
  register: treesitter_version_check
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false

- name: Verify tree-sitter native binary is non-empty + executable
  # tree-sitter-cli's postinstall download can fail silently, leaving an
  # empty 0-byte native binary (mode 0600). `--version` still reports OK
  # (it only reads package.json), so the cheap check passes — but every
  # `:TSInstall`/parser build explodes with EACCES on spawn. Re-check
  # the resolved binary to catch this.
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
    - treesitter_version_check.rc == 0
  ansible.builtin.shell: |
    set -e
    bin=$(PATH="${HOME}/.cargo/bin:${PATH}" command -v tree-sitter)
    # resolve symlinks (mise shim → mise bin → cli.js; cli.js spawns ./tree-sitter)
    real_cli=$(readlink -f "$bin")
    native="$(dirname "$real_cli")/tree-sitter"
    # cli.js lives next to the native binary in tree-sitter-cli/
    [[ -s "$native" ]] && [[ -x "$native" ]]
  args: { executable: /bin/bash }
  register: treesitter_native_check
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false

- name: Compute treesitter_check aggregate
  ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    treesitter_check:
      rc: >-
        {{ 0 if (treesitter_version_check.rc | default(1) == 0
                 and treesitter_native_check.rc | default(1) == 0)
           else 1 }}

- name: Purge broken empty tree-sitter native binary (if present)
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
    - treesitter_version_check.rc | default(1) == 0
    - treesitter_native_check.rc | default(1) != 0
  ansible.builtin.shell: |
    set -e
    bin=$(PATH="${HOME}/.cargo/bin:${PATH}" command -v tree-sitter)
    real_cli=$(readlink -f "$bin")
    native="$(dirname "$real_cli")/tree-sitter"
    if [[ -e "$native" && ! -s "$native" ]]; then
      rm -f "$native"
      echo "removed empty tree-sitter native binary: $native"
    fi
  args: { executable: /bin/bash }
  changed_when: "'removed' in (treesitter_native_purge.stdout | default(''))"
  register: treesitter_native_purge
\```

Downstream tasks already gate on `treesitter_check.rc != 0` (lines 246, 267, 284, 300) — no edits needed to the npm/cargo install paths. After the fact construction above, those gates resolve correctly.

### Immediate manual recovery (not part of plan file — user runs these outside plan mode)

\```bash
rm -f ~/.local/share/mise/installs/node/24.13.0/lib/node_modules/tree-sitter-cli/tree-sitter
mise exec -- npm install -g tree-sitter-cli
# if that fails (e.g. postinstall download still blocked), fall back:
cargo install tree-sitter-cli
\```

Then in Neovim: `:TSInstall! all` (or just let it retry on open).

## Approved Plan:
# `chezmoi apply` on jingle-207 (noRoot=true): two bugs

## Context

On `jingle-207` (Ubuntu 22.04, ubuntu_server profile, **noRoot=true**), `chezmoi apply` fails with two independent issues:

1. **ansible task hits `sudo: a password is required`** at `devtools : Ensure xz is available for worktrunk extraction (Debian/Ubuntu)` even though the machine is in noRoot mode. Root cause: that task is missing the `tags: [sudo]` annotation, so `ansible-playbook --skip-tags sudo` (the mechanism this repo uses to honor noRoot) doesn't skip it. Exit status 2 from `run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh` aborts the whole `chezmoi apply`.

2. **Neovim `nvim-treesitter` parser builds fail with `EACCES`** on every language. The native tree-sitter binary at `/home/ldw/.local/share/mise/installs/node/24.13.0/lib/node_modules/tree-sitter-cli/tree-sitter` is a **0-byte file with mode `0600`** (neither executable nor has any content). Caused by an earlier `npm install -g tree-sitter-cli` whose postinstall `install.js` download stream silently failed (GitHub release CDN → Azure blob is flaky behind GFW), leaving the empty file behind. Ansible's detection is too weak to notice: `treesitter_check` runs `tree-sitter --version`, which in `cli.js` just reads `package.json` — it exits `0` reporting `0.26.8` without ever touching the broken native binary. So every re-apply happily skips the reinstall.

Both are broad "install path is too optimistic about success / too naive about capability" bugs, so the fix for each is a small guard in the same ansible role.

No doc updates required under `docs/` or `README.md` — pure ansible-internal guards, not a user-facing surface change.

No CLAUDE.md update required — bug fix, not a cross-file invariant. (If either pitfall later recurs on other hosts or silently corrupts state, CLAUDE.md's pitfalls-graduation rule says promote to a Hard invariant; not yet.)

### New pitfalls (symptom-titled, verbatim errors, per CLAUDE.md pitfalls rules)

**`pitfalls/ansible-missing-sudo-tag.md`** — title: _"`chezmoi apply` in noRoot mode fails at `Ensure xz is available for worktrunk extraction` with `sudo: a password is required`"_

Body outline:
- Verbatim error: `Task failed: Premature end of stream waiting for become success. / sudo: a password is required` at `roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml:2415`.
- Why: noRoot mode is implemented as `ansible-playbook --skip-tags sudo` (not an ansible var). Any task with `become: true` must ALSO declare `tags: [sudo]` or it escapes the skip filter and the sudoers prompt hard-fails a non-interactive run.
- How it hides: works fine on rooted dev boxes (the machines the author usually tests on), breaks only on server profile + noRoot.
- Non-obvious workaround / convention: grep precedent — `jnv` xz task at `roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml:3115–3124` is the canonical pattern. Any new `become: true` in an ansible role in this repo MUST be paired with `tags: [sudo]`.
- Detection for future audits: `rg -U 'become: true(?![^-]*tags: \[sudo\])' dot_ansible/` (crude, will have false positives around handlers — still a useful sanity pass).

**`pitfalls/tree-sitter-cli-empty-native-binary.md`** — title: _"nvim-treesitter `:TSInstall` fails on every language with `spawn …/tree-sitter-cli/tree-sitter EACCES` even though `tree-sitter --version` reports a version"_

Body outline:
- Verbatim error (multi-line, include the Node.js stack so future-me grep-finds it):
  ```
  Error: spawn /home/…/mise/installs/node/…/lib/node_modules/tree-sitter-cli/tree-sitter EACCES
      errno: -13, code: 'EACCES',
      syscall: 'spawn …/tree-sitter-cli/tree-sitter',
      spawnargs: [ 'build', '-o', 'parser.so' ]
  ```
- Why: tree-sitter-cli's npm `postinstall` (`install.js`) downloads a prebuilt Linux binary from GitHub release-assets (Azure blob CDN). Behind GFW / on flaky network the gunzip stream fails silently, leaving a **0-byte file with mode `0600`** next to `cli.js`, and the process still exits 0. `tree-sitter --version` returns fine because cli.js reads `package.json` without ever touching the native binary — so ansible's version probe sees a healthy install and skips the reinstall. Every `:TSInstall` / `:TSUpdate` then explodes because each parser build does `spawn('./tree-sitter', ['build', …])`.
- Non-obvious fix: detect via `[[ -s $native && -x $native ]]` not `--version`.
- Recovery recipe: `rm` the empty binary, then `mise exec -- npm install -g tree-sitter-cli` (or `cargo install tree-sitter-cli` if the CDN is still unreachable — TUNA mirror for crates works behind GFW).
- Symptom that misleads: `tree-sitter 0.26.8` printed correctly → easy to rule out "tree-sitter not installed" and chase nvim config instead. Spent real time here.

---

## Verification

After applying the ansible changes on jingle-207 (or any noRoot Ubuntu host):

1. **Worktrunk xz path**:
   ```bash
   chezmoi apply  # should now pass through the worktrunk section
   ```
   Expect in the output:
   - `Ensure xz is available for worktrunk extraction` → `skipped` (tag filter)
   - `Probe for xz binary (worktrunk extraction dependency)` → `ok`
   - `Install worktrunk from GitHub releases …` → `skipped` (xz probe empty)
   - `wt` absent from `~/.local/bin` — acceptable in noRoot mode.

   On a host that DOES have xz (linuxbrew, docker/CI, rooted box), the install block runs and `wt --version` works after.

2. **Tree-sitter detection**:
   On the current broken jingle-207, after manual recovery above, re-run:
   ```bash
   chezmoi apply
   ```
   Then intentionally break it again to exercise the new guard:
   ```bash
   : > ~/.local/share/mise/installs/node/24.13.0/lib/node_modules/tree-sitter-cli/tree-sitter
   chmod 600 ~/.local/share/mise/installs/node/24.13.0/lib/node_modules/tree-sitter-cli/tree-sitter
   chezmoi apply
   ```
   Expect:
   - `Check if tree-sitter --version works` → `ok` (rc 0)
   - `Verify tree-sitter native binary is non-empty + executable` → `ok` but `rc != 0`
   - `Purge broken empty tree-sitter native binary` → `changed`
   - `Install tree-sitter-cli via mise npm` → `changed` (reinstall fires)
   - After apply, `nvim +'TSInstall! bash' +qa` completes with no EACCES spam.

3. **No regression on healthy hosts**: on any host where tree-sitter already works (not 0-bytes), the version check is `ok rc 0`, the native check is `ok rc 0`, aggregate `rc = 0`, reinstall is skipped. Same observable behavior as today.

1	# Pitfalls
2	
3	Past traps we've stepped on. Symptoms-first knowledge base — the goal is that
4	when a problem recurs (on a new machine, after an upgrade, with a new tool
5	combo), grepping the symptom here lands you on the root cause and workaround
6	in seconds, instead of re-debugging from scratch.
7	
8	This folder is `chezmoi`-ignored (see `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` → `pitfalls/**`); it
9	is repo metadata for maintainers, not user-facing config to deploy.
10	
11	## Pitfalls vs the rest
12	
13	This repo has four sibling surfaces with overlapping shapes; pick the right one:
14	
15	| Surface | Time direction | Question it answers | Access pattern |
16	|---|---|---|---|
17	| `docs/tools/<tool>.md` | Present | "How does this tool work / how do I configure it?" | Read top to bottom |
18	| `docs/this_repo/<topic>.md` | Present | "Why did we architect it this way?" | Read top to bottom |
19	| `pitfalls/<slug>.md` | **Past** | **"I see error X — has this happened before?"** | **Grep symptoms** |
20	| `backlog/<slug>.md` | Future | "We thought about doing Y — what was the analysis?" | Index in `TODO.md` |
21	| `AGENTS.md` Hard invariants | Present | "What rules MUST agents follow?" | Read top to bottom |
22	
23	A pitfall **graduates** to a Hard invariant in `AGENTS.md` when the trap is
24	serious enough that you can't rely on memory or grep — typically when (a) it
25	recurs across machines, (b) it silently corrupts state, or (c) the workaround
26	is non-obvious and easy to undo by accident. When graduating, leave a
27	`pitfalls/<slug>.md` as historical record and link to it from the invariant.
28	
29	## When to add a pitfall doc
30	
31	Add a `pitfalls/<slug>.md` when you've spent more than ~15 minutes on something
32	where the answer wasn't googleable, AND any of:
33	
34	- The symptom is non-obvious from the root cause (`SSH_CONNECTION` cleared
35	  silently → hostname module disappears, no error)
36	- The fix is "do nothing different but in a specific order" (sentinel writes
37	  must come after `wait $pid` for fleet-apply, etc.)
38	- The same trap could be hit by a new agent / new machine / new contributor
39	- An upstream bug exists with no ETA — workaround needs to outlive memory
40	- A specific tool version is required (or forbidden) and the failure mode at
41	  the wrong version is silent / confusing (e.g. tmux 3.2a popup off-screen)
42	
43	## When NOT to add a pitfall doc
44	
45	- Trivially googleable error (the next person will solve in 30 seconds anyway)
46	- Already covered in `docs/tools/<tool>.md` as part of the tool's normal
47	  configuration — cross-link from this README's "Cross-referenced pitfalls"
48	  table below instead of duplicating
49	- Already a `AGENTS.md` Hard invariant — those have higher priority enforcement
50	  (cross-link only)
51	- One-off transient (network glitch, machine-specific config rot) — fix and
52	  move on
53	
54	## File template
55	
56	See [`assets/pitfall-doc.md.template`](#) in the
57	[`project-knowledge-harness` skill](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/tree/main/skills/local/project-knowledge-harness),
58	or copy the structure of an existing entry below.
59	
60	Key sections (different from `backlog/` template — symptom-first, not
61	context-first):
62	
63	```markdown
64	# <Title describing the SYMPTOM, not the root cause>
65	
66	**Symptoms** (grep this section): <verbatim error messages, observable behaviour>
67	**First seen**: YYYY-MM
68	**Affects**: <tool/version/OS combo>
69	**Status**: workaround documented / fixed upstream in vX.Y / WONTFIX
70	
71	## Symptom
72	
73	Full error messages (verbatim, not paraphrased — preserves grep-ability).
74	Reproduction steps if applicable.
75	
76	## Root cause
77	
78	Why this happens. Reference source, docs, or upstream issue.
79	
80	## Workaround
81	
82	Immediate workaround (commands, config diff). Should be copy-pasteable.
83	
84	## Prevention
85	
86	How to avoid stepping on this again. If serious enough, link to the
87	corresponding `AGENTS.md` Hard invariant.
88	
89	## Related
90	
91	Links to `docs/`, sibling pitfalls, `TODO.md` entries (if a real fix is
92	queued), upstream issues/PRs.
93	```
94

110	| [`yazi-tmux-popup-crash`](yazi-tmux-popup-crash.md) | Yazi inside `display-popup` crashes tmux server, "Terminal response timeout" | workaround documented |
111	| [`zsh-tied-array-path-shadowing`](zsh-tied-array-path-shadowing.md) | `command not found` only inside one zsh function, works at prompt; `hash -r` / `rehash` doesn't help | fixed in `dot_config/zsh/tools/22_sesh.zsh` (rename local `path` → `target`) |
112	| [`tmux-resurrect-agents`](tmux-resurrect-agents.md) | reattach restores layout but agent/TUI panes come back as bare shell | workaround documented (`@resurrect-processes` whitelist) |
113	| [`yazi-tmux-popup-crash`](yazi-tmux-popup-crash.md) | `Terminal response timeout` from yazi → tmux server dies | workaround documented (use `new-window`, not `display-popup`) |

```text
1	# `npm install -g <pkg>` hangs forever after "Downloading https://github.com/.../releases/..."
2	
3	**Symptoms** (grep this section):
4	- `npm install -g tree-sitter-cli` hangs indefinitely on a fresh China-based
5	  (GFW) host
6	- Last visible output: `Downloading https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter/releases/download/vX.Y.Z/tree-sitter-linux-x64.gz`
7	- `npm http fetch GET 200 https://registry.npmmirror.com/...` succeeds (so npm
8	  registry mirror IS working)
9	- `ansible-playbook` task `Install tree-sitter-cli via mise npm` never returns;
10	  whole `chezmoi apply` runs over `command_timeout` budget (2 hours)
11	- `pgrep -lf "node install"` shows `node install.js` stuck; `strace -p <pid>`
12	  shows it `read(socket, ...)` blocked
13	- `ssh HOST pstree -p $PID` shows `chezmoi → ansible-playbook → … → node install.js`
14	
15	**First seen**: 2026-04 on `jingle207` (Ubuntu 22.04, China network, useChineseMirror=true)
16	**Affects**: any npm package whose `postinstall` script downloads a prebuilt
17	binary directly from `github.com/.../releases/download/...` — confirmed for
18	`tree-sitter-cli`, suspected for any node-gyp prebuilt fallback path
19	**Status**: workaround in place (`timeout 180` + cargo fallback in
20	`dot_ansible/roles/lazyvim_deps/tasks/main.yml`); no upstream fix expected
21	(tree-sitter install.js hardcodes the URL, no env-var override)
22	
23	## Symptom
24	
25	After running `chezmoi apply` (or `just fleet-apply`) on a fresh Ubuntu host
26	in China, the apply hangs at:
27	
28	```
29	[27] TASK · [lazyvim_deps : Check if tree-sitter is installed]
30	ok: [localhost] (0.5s)
31	[28] TASK · [lazyvim_deps : Install tree-sitter-cli via mise npm (Debian/Ubuntu)]
32	```
33	
34	Drill in:
35	
36	```bash
37	ssh HOST pgrep -lf "tree-sitter|node install|npm install tre"
38	# 1539421 npm install tre
39	# 1539702 sh
40	# 1539703 MainThread
41	```
42	
43	Reproduce manually:
44	
45	```bash
46	ssh HOST 'mise exec -- npm install -g tree-sitter-cli --loglevel=http' &
47	# After ~30s, output stops at:
48	# npm http fetch GET 200 https://registry.npmmirror.com/tree-sitter-cli 123ms (cache revalidated)
49	# (then nothing — postinstall hangs)
50	```
51	
52	Force the postinstall to error fast to see what it's doing:
53	
54	```bash
55	ssh HOST 'timeout 30 mise exec -- npm install -g tree-sitter-cli 2>&1 | tail -10'
56	# npm error signal SIGTERM
57	# npm error command sh -c node install.js
58	# npm error Downloading https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter/releases/download/v0.26.8/tree-sitter-linux-x64.gz
59	```
60	
61	## Root cause
62	
63	`tree-sitter-cli`'s `package.json` has a `postinstall` script that runs
64	`node install.js`. The script (verbatim, from the package):
65	
66	```js
67	const releaseURL = `https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter/releases/download/v${packageJSON.version}`;
68	const assetName = `tree-sitter-${platform.name}-${arch.name}.gz`;
69	const assetURL = `${releaseURL}/${assetName}`;
70	// ...
71	get(assetURL, response => { ... });
72	```
73	
74	The URL is **hardcoded**. There is no `TREE_SITTER_BINARY_URL`,
75	`TREE_SITTER_MIRROR`, or any environment-variable override.
76	
77	`github.com` itself is reachable from China (HTTP 200 with reasonable
78	latency), but it issues a 302 redirect to
79	`release-assets.githubusercontent.com` — Azure blob storage — which is
80	frequently unreachable or extremely slow from Chinese networks. The Node
81	HTTPS client has no default timeout, so the connection hangs indefinitely
82	in `read()` waiting for the TLS handshake or first byte.
83	
84	Why the npm tarball mirror doesn't help: `registry.npmmirror.com` mirrors
85	the npm package itself (the `.tgz` containing JS files, including
86	`install.js`). It does NOT mirror the `tree-sitter` binary releases (those
87	are published to GitHub Releases, not to npm). npmmirror's binary mirror
88	namespace (`/-/binary/`) only covers ~99 well-known projects (Node.js,
89	Electron, Chromium, etc.); tree-sitter is not on the list.
90	
91	Why ansible's `ignore_errors: true` doesn't save you: it only catches
92	non-zero exit. A hang has no exit code — the task just sits in `running`
93	state until ansible's external timeout (none by default) or fleet-apply's
94	outer `command_timeout` kicks in (2h default).
95	
96	## Workaround
97	
98	Wrap the npm install with `timeout(1)` and trigger a `cargo install` fallback
99	on non-zero exit (timeout exits 124, which is non-zero):
100	
101	```yaml
102	- name: Install tree-sitter-cli via mise npm (Debian/Ubuntu)
103	  ansible.builtin.shell: |
104	    timeout 180 {{ mise_bin }} exec -- npm install -g tree-sitter-cli
105	  args:
106	    executable: /bin/bash
107	  register: treesitter_npm
108	  changed_when: "'added' in treesitter_npm.stdout or 'added' in treesitter_npm.stderr"
109	  failed_when: false  # Don't kill the play; cargo fallback handles it.
110	
111	- name: Install tree-sitter-cli via cargo (fallback)
112	  when:
113	    - treesitter_npm.rc | default(1) != 0  # Catches both fail AND timeout 124.
114	  ansible.builtin.shell: |
115	    cargo install tree-sitter-cli
116	```
117	
118	Why cargo works behind GFW:
119	
120	- `crates.io` is mirrored via TUNA sparse index (configured in
121	  `~/.cargo/config.toml` when `useChineseMirror=true`)
122	- `cargo install` builds from source on the local machine — no GitHub
123	  Releases roundtrip
124	- All transitive deps come through the same TUNA mirror
125	
126	Cost: ~3-5 min build time vs ~30s for the prebuilt binary, plus
127	`libclang-dev` apt dep (also installed by the role).
128	
129	Manual one-shot fix on a host that's already stuck:
130	
131	```bash
132	# Kill the hung npm process tree
133	ssh HOST 'pkill -9 -f "npm install -g tree-sitter-cli"; pkill -9 -f "node install.js"'
134	
135	# Install via cargo using the right rustc (mise's, not system 1.75):
136	ssh HOST 'mise exec -- cargo install tree-sitter-cli'
137	
138	# Verify
139	ssh HOST '~/.cargo/bin/tree-sitter --version'
140	```
141	
142	## Prevention
143	
144	When adding a new ansible task that runs `npm install -g <package>`:
145	
146	1. **Check for postinstall binary downloads** before merging:
147	
148	   ```bash
149	   npm view <package> scripts.postinstall
150	   # Or read the package's install.js / preinstall.js
151	   ```
152	
153	   If the script `https.get` from `github.com/.../releases/`, you're at
154	   risk on GFW hosts.
155	
156	2. **Always wrap with `timeout`**, even if the package looks safe today
157	   — postinstall scripts can be added in a minor release. Pick a
158	   timeout that's 3-5x the expected install time on a working network.
159	
160	3. **Provide a fallback** — usually `cargo install`, `apt install`, or
161	   manual binary download from a mirrored host (npmmirror's
162	   `/-/binary/` namespace, conda-forge, etc.).
163	
164	4. **Use `failed_when: false` + explicit `rc` gate**, not `ignore_errors:
165	   true`. The latter masks the failure but keeps the task `ok` in
166	   recap, hiding the fact that the fallback fired.
167	
168	5. **Consider whether npm is even the right install method.** For
169	   tree-sitter specifically, `cargo install` works on every platform
170	   without GFW concerns; the npm path only exists because it's faster
171	   on a clean network. If you don't care about install speed, skip npm
172	   entirely.
173	
174	## Related
175	
176	- [docs/tools/mirrors.md → npm postinstall scripts](../docs/tools/mirrors.md#npm-postinstall-scripts-that-download-from-github-releases)
177	  — coverage matrix and adding-new-tasks checklist
178	- [docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md → When a host hangs](../docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md#when-a-host-hangs)
179	  — recovery flow when this (or a similar) hang manifests as a stuck
180	  fleet-apply run
181	- [tree-sitter/tree-sitter-cli install.js](https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter/blob/master/cli/npm/install.js)
182	  — upstream source confirming hardcoded URL
183
```
